summary: Task 8 rewrite is structurally correct: WebClient/Mono/Flux/StepVerifier symbols are gone from all 5 files, public statics (DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT, CONNECT_TIMEOUT, requireValidTokenShape, isTransient, scrubTokens) are preserved, audit ordering and the AtomicInteger semantics (single increment per RestClient request, persisting across both loops) are implemented per spec, and every prior test scenario is preserved 1:1 with sensible name updates (nettyReadTimeout → readTimeout). However, sleepWithDeadline does not clamp Thread.sleep to the remaining budget, which breaks the 429-large-retry-after overall-timeout test invariant and degrades production behavior: a single 429 with retry_after ~30s will block for the full 30s even when the overall 30s budget has only seconds left. This is a critical deviation from spec line 24 ("overall 30s timeout enforced") and the test at TelegramSenderTest.java:339-355 (asserts elapsedMs < 8000 under SHORT_OVERALL_TIMEOUT=3s with retry_after=120 clamped to 30).

criticalIssues.issue:
sleepWithDeadline(durationMs, deadline, attempts) calls Thread.sleep(durationMs) without clamping to the remaining budget. The pre-sleep checkDeadline only fires if the deadline is ALREADY past; it does not prevent a sleep that will overshoot the deadline. The post-sleep check then fires after the overshoot, so the timeout signal is correct but the wall-clock budget is blown.

Concrete failure mode (test TelegramSenderTest.java:339-355, sendText_429LargeRetryAfter_capsAtOverallTimeout):
  - SHORT_OVERALL_TIMEOUT = 3s, deadline captured at t=0 ⇒ deadline = t+3s.
  - First HTTP attempt (~50ms) returns 429 with retry_after=120 ⇒ clamp(120, 30) = 30s sleep.
  - sleepWithDeadline(30000+jitter, deadline=3s, attempts):
      • checkDeadline at t≈100ms ⇒ not expired, passes.
      • Thread.sleep(30000+jitter) ⇒ blocks for 30s.
      • checkDeadline at t≈30100ms ⇒ throws TelegramSendException("timeout").
  - Total elapsed ≈ 30s. Test asserts elapsedMs < 8000 ⇒ FAILS once Wave 2 closes and tests run.

Production impact: with the spec'd 30s overallTimeout, a 429 received late in the budget (say, after ~25s consumed by 5xx retries) still blocks the calling VT for up to 30s on Thread.sleep — total 55s wall-clock — even though the deadline says to abandon at 30s. Carrier-thread parking under VT is cheap, but the caller (BotService / webhook job) still waits ~55s before seeing the timeout exception.
criticalIssues.impact: 1) Test sendText_429LargeRetryAfter_capsAtOverallTimeout will fail its < 8000ms timing assertion at the next ./gradlew test run (after Task 9/10 unblock it). 2) Production callers will observe wall-clock latency up to overallTimeout + 30s (instead of ≤ overallTimeout) for any sendText that hits a 429 with non-trivial retry_after late in the budget. 3) Violates tech-spec line 203 ("check deadline BEFORE the sleep (avoid an unnecessary sleep that would overshoot)") — current implementation only avoids sleep when deadline is ALREADY past, not when the sleep itself would overshoot.

suggestions.suggestion: Doc comment still references the deleted reactive architecture: "internal to TelegramSender's .retryWhen filter (Decision 5 / Architecture step 11)". Post-Task-8 there is no .retryWhen — the exception is now propagated from the 4xx handler (TelegramSender.map4xx line 266) out of sendWith5xxRetry's re-throw branch (line 169-171) into sendWithRateLimitRetry's catch (line 151). Update to: "Package-private on purpose: this exception is internal to TelegramSender's nested-loop retry logic — propagated from the 4xx handler (map4xx) through the inner 5xx loop's re-throw branch into the outer 429 retry loop. Never reaches GlobalErrorHandler."
suggestions.benefit: Removes stale Reactor references that will confuse future readers; preserves the design-intent comment.

suggestions.suggestion: Class-level Javadoc still says "decrypted token is captured in a local variable for the duration of one HTTP attempt and reachable until the synchronous call returns" — accurate now but the prior sentence "Plaintext-token lifetime" was rewritten well. Consider also dropping the "Never... pushed to background schedulers" clause: under VT there is no scheduler hop, so the sentence reads oddly. Optional.
suggestions.benefit: Cleaner doc; matches the synchronous reality.

suggestions.suggestion: The Optional<Bot> botOpt local variable can be inlined: Bot bot = botRepository.findById(botId).filter(b -> b.getStatus() == BotStatus.CONNECTED).orElseThrow(() -> AppException.notFound(MESSAGE_BOT_NOT_FOUND)); — collapses two lines into one without losing clarity. The two-line form is fine if you prefer to keep the .filter readable; this is a pure style nit.

mapBodyToSentMessage now handles result == null with a separate warn ("Telegram ok=false or missing message_id: null body") and throws TelegramSendException(null, "null body", ...). This is a defensive ADD vs the prior Reactor pipeline (which silently dropped null via flatMap). The added branch is correct and strictly stricter, but the warn message string "null body" is a literal — consider using a constant or comment so the log line's intent is documented (today a reader sees a literal "null body" string and may wonder if it's user-controlled).
suggestions.benefit: Easier to grep for the specific log site; less ambiguity about whether the string is user-supplied.

suggestions.suggestion: sendText_tokenInTerminalFailureLog_scrubbed_errorLevel only asserts noneMatch(TOKEN) on error logs — the comment explicitly explains why a positive [REDACTED_TOKEN] match is omitted (the terminal ERROR log emits the sentinel "transient_failure_exhausted" not the original 5xx body). That's correct reasoning, but it leaves the test vulnerable to a regression where the terminal ERROR site forgets to call scrubTokens entirely — the negative-only assertion would still pass if the formatted message contains *any* non-token-shaped substring. Consider adding a complementary positive assertion: assertThat(errorMessages).anyMatch(m -> m.contains("Telegram send terminal failure")) to at least pin the log-site format string.
suggestions.benefit: Stronger regression net for the terminal-failure log site; complements the per-site TC10 invariant.

suggestions.suggestion: sendText_botNotFound_throwsNotFound_noHttp does not assert verify(eventService, never()).logEvent(...). The implementation correctly skips audit on AppException(404) via isTerminalAuditable, but the test only checks getRequestCount()==0. Adding verify(eventService, never()).logEvent(any(), any(), any(), any(), any()) would lock the no-audit invariant for the bot-not-found / disconnected paths (the same applies to sendText_botDisconnected at line 568). Same gap existed pre-Task-8 — not a regression, but cheap to close while you're here.
suggestions.benefit: Closes a gap in the no-audit invariant for pre-HTTP 404 paths; cheap to add.

suggestions.suggestion: Task spec line 93 (sendText_terminalFailure_emitsErrorLogBeforeAuditEvent) mentions verifying ordering via InOrder on appender + eventService. The current tests (e.g. sendText_5xxRetryExhausted at line 268 and sendText_tokenInTerminalFailureLog at line 681) verify BOTH the error log and the audit event exist, but do not strictly enforce the log-before-event temporal ordering. Code-level ordering is correct (TelegramSender:134-137 explicitly orders log.error → logEvent → throw), but a regression where a future refactor swaps the order would not be caught. Consider adding an InOrder verification in one terminal-failure test to lock the ordering invariant.
suggestions.benefit: Codifies the audit-ordering invariant called out in tech-spec line 50 / task line 93; future refactors cannot silently regress it.
